source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use a U-100 insulin syringe for U-100 insulin to minimize unit-to-volume dosing errors","B":"Use any one-milliliter syringe because insulin units and milliliters are interchangeable","C":"Use a tuberculin syringe routinely without a prescribed unit-to-volume conversion plan","D":"Select the syringe only by needle length because barrel calibration does not affect dosing"}}
source_row.rationale: U-100 insulin syringes are calibrated in insulin units for 100 units/mL insulin and reduce the need for manual unit-to-volume conversion. A tuberculin syringe measures milliliters, so routine substitution without explicit professional conversion instructions creates avoidable dosing-error risk.
source_row.source_detail: Dosage/administration and device instructions: U-100 insulin is measured in units with compatible U-100 delivery devices; mismatched volume/unit conversion can cause dosing error; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client uses U-100 insulin and asks whether an old 1 mL tuberculin syringe can routinely replace a U-100 insulin syringe for self-administration. Which teaching is safest?
